[Nature Biotechnology · 2024]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### The global patent landscape of phage therapy

Phage therapy uses viruses that kill bacteria, and it is gaining attention as antibiotics fail. This study maps who patents phage therapies, in which countries, and how the field is changing, using machine learning on large patent datasets.

[Patents]{.tag} [Infectious disease]{.tag} [Machine learning]{.tag}

[Read the article](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-024-02493-9)
:::
:::

::: {.work-item .reveal}
[Sample report · Patents]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### Immune checkpoint therapy: patent intelligence

A patent study of one of the most active areas in cancer treatment: the leading inventors and applicants, collaboration networks, and the countries where new innovation is growing. It comes with an interactive dashboard.

[Patents]{.tag} [Networks]{.tag} [Dashboard]{.tag}

[Explore the dashboard](dashboards/immune-checkpoint.qmd)
:::
:::

::: {.work-item .reveal}
[In progress · Global health]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### Ticks, climate and research equity

Ticks spread diseases that affect people and animals, and climate change is moving them to new places. This study looks at research on ticks worldwide, with a focus on Africa: who produces it, who leads it, and who funds it.

[Global health]{.tag} [Africa]{.tag} [Equity]{.tag}
:::
:::
